newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade moderate $63-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade moderate $63-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle on Monday sold at $63.00 per cwt in moderate trading, unchanged from light sales late last week, feedlot sources said.
About 18,500 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and an estimated 100 steers sold in Kansas, the sources said.

The sales come on the heels of last week's large volume, which was so active that owners, anxious to remain current in their marketings, dipped into this week's showlists to sell as many cattle as possible, they said.
Fed cattle prices were underpinned by brisk beef sales last week, with Friday's daily movement "one of the largest ever for a Friday," said Dave Maher, livestock analyst with Securities Corp of Iowa.
Fabricated beef movement Friday was 445 loads, which brought weekly sales to 1,654, the second largest of the year, behind 1,735 loads the week ended March 14, USDA statistics showed.
Showlists were estimated lower than last week, but there still remained a large number of market-ready cattle, which could weigh on prices later this week, market sources said.
Showlists in the Panhandle were pegged near 80,500 head, down 6,000 from last week and the Kansas showlist was estimated near 89,000, down 5,000.
